headline: Binder design targets antigen variants, peptide latent spaces and simulated binding data
label: Computational Binder Design
summary: Recent preprints move binder design beyond single-target affinity toward multi-variant, latent-space and data-scarcity objectives.
synthesis: The common thread is binder design conditioned on objectives beyond affinity to one fixed target. Germinal Multi jointly optimizes one antibody paratope against multiple antigen variants, yielding designs that bind EGFR variants and neutralize SARS-CoV-2. The PDZ-binding study designs peptide motifs by moving along directions in a shared PDZ-PBM latent space learned from affinity prediction. VReceptor addresses data scarcity by generating sequence-dependent peptide binding data through pharmacophore-inspired weighting. What is new is the shift from static, single-target optimization toward evolving antigens, latent-space navigation and simulated training data. Modalities and validation standards differ across these preprints, so their results are not directly comparable.
